summary: Ported the previously SM90-validated TileLang raw-FP8 KV plumbing from upstream PR #36904 onto current main. CUDA SM89+ now accepts fp8_e4m3 only when both DSA backends are TileLang, selects the raw MLA layout, uses the raw fused-quant writer, dispatches the existing FP8 partial kernel, and disables the scaled-layout MHA one-shot path. Mixed backends, pre-SM89 GPUs, and DCP remain rejected.

tests.what_was_measured: 10 validation and layout regressions passed, including SM90 acceptance and mixed-backend, pre-SM89, DCP, HIP, BF16, non-TileLang, raw-layout, and scaled-layout boundaries.

10 CPU regressions passed; the two CUDA SM89+ numerical tests were collected and skipped on the assigned ROCm host. They cover one-hot exactness, an FP32 reference tolerance, and a scrambled-index negative control.
9 selected tests plus 6 subtests passed against the current backend-resolution pipeline.
All modified Python implementation modules compiled successfully.

tests.what_was_measured: The assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950, HIP 7.2) was detected, but the prepared TileLang/TVM compiler failed during layout inference with an internal divide-by-zero before kernel launch.

gpu_execution_evidence: A real gfx950 compilation attempt was made, but no GPU kernel executed because TileLang/TVM failed before launch. The issue's CUDA SM90 path cannot run on the assigned ROCm GPU.
remaining_limitations: No CUDA SM90 GPU or GLM-5.3-Flash weights were available, so the current-tree patch was not exercised end to end on the reported 8xH20 workload.
The implementation is based on upstream PR #36904, whose same raw-layout approach was independently reported successful on 8xH20/SM90, but that PR closed without merging.
The assigned gfx950 numerical probe was blocked by a prepared TileLang/TVM compiler internal error before launch; no ROCm numerical result is claimed.
No full-model, semantic-accuracy, speculative-decoding, multi-GPU, or multi-node claim is made.
